An interest in systems shaped by Computer Science, aviation learning, and technology events.

  • I study Computer Science alongside Mathematics and Physics at International A Level. Outside school, aviation courses and events helped me become interested in how separate components, people, and decisions contribute to one outcome. My later technology reflections extend that interest into AI, cybersecurity, identity, and business.
  • In my Global Airports Forum post, I described how a short boarding delay can connect to gate availability, crew duty time, aircraft rotations, baggage, and wider coordination. The observation changed how I looked at something that can appear simple from the passenger’s perspective.
  • At Money20/20, I wrote about AI agents and questions of identity and authorisation. At the UNESCO forum, I focused on responsibility and governance. Those experiences shifted my attention from what technology can demonstrate to what organisations need before they can rely on it.
  • This portfolio itself applies a small version of that approach. Content, evidence, navigation, reading modes, and accessibility need to support one another. A feature that looks attractive but hides useful information would work against the site’s purpose.
01 / 04

Where the interest comes from

I study Computer Science alongside Mathematics and Physics at International A Level.

Outside school, aviation courses and events helped me become interested in how separate components, people, and decisions contribute to one outcome. My later technology reflections extend that interest into AI, cybersecurity, identity, and business.

The connection

This page describes a way of approaching learning, rather than a formally assessed skill on my LinkedIn profile.

Read the deeper context+

Systems thinking is the connection between these experiences: looking at the wider context instead of treating an impressive result as self-explanatory.

02 / 04

The airport example

In my Global Airports Forum post, I described how a short boarding delay can connect to gate availability, crew duty time, aircraft rotations, baggage, and wider coordination.

The observation changed how I looked at something that can appear simple from the passenger’s perspective.

The connection

The useful habit is to ask what dependencies sit behind an outcome.

Read the deeper context+

Which teams need to coordinate? Which information arrives at the right time? What happens when one assumption changes? These questions encourage a more careful account of a system without pretending to have operational expertise.

03 / 04

The technology example

At Money20/20, I wrote about AI agents and questions of identity and authorisation.

At the UNESCO forum, I focused on responsibility and governance. Those experiences shifted my attention from what technology can demonstrate to what organisations need before they can rely on it.

The connection

That distinction is relevant to my current commercial interests.

Read the deeper context+

A business adopting a new tool has more to consider than a feature list. I want to understand the human, organisational, and technical context around the decision, while recognising that specialist conclusions require deeper knowledge.

04 / 04

Applying the habit carefully

This portfolio itself applies a small version of that approach.

Content, evidence, navigation, reading modes, and accessibility need to support one another. A feature that looks attractive but hides useful information would work against the site’s purpose.

The connection

My next development step is to make those connections clearer in research and writing.

Read the deeper context+

I want to identify assumptions, describe dependencies, and keep the limits of my understanding visible. The result should be a better question and a more useful explanation, not an inflated technical title.

Source context

Profile facts were reviewed on 6 October 2026. Expanded prose provides personal and learning context; listed achievements remain separate from future ambitions.
